transcript:
Agent: Thank you for calling card customer service. My name is Julian. How can I help you today?
Customer: Hi, I'm calling about an issue with a charge from a mechanic on my recent bill.
Agent: I can certainly assist you with looking into that. May I have your full name and your billing zip code, please?
Customer: Yes, it's Harriet Osei, and the zip is 43215.
Agent: Thank you, Ms. Osei. Could you tell me the name of the business and the total that was charged?
Customer: The business is Millbrook Auto Care. It's on my September 23, 2026 statement for $1,480.00.
Agent: Got it. And what date did the transaction take place?
Customer: That was back on September 13, 2026.
Agent: Could you walk me through what happened with this transaction?
Customer: I brought my car in to have some brake work done. They gave me a written quote for $1,150, but then they charged $1,480.00 to my card without calling me first.
Agent: Did you speak with the shop about the difference when you picked up the vehicle?
Customer: I did, and the person at the desk just said the parts were more expensive than they thought. But nobody checked with me before doing the work.
Agent: Do you still have a copy of the written quote they provided?
Customer: Yes, I kept the paper quote they printed out for me when I dropped off the car.
Agent: Did you sign any paperwork or give permission over the phone for the total to go above the $1,150?
Customer: No, I didn't sign anything else and no one contacted me to approve anything higher.
Agent: So you have a written quote for $1,150 from Millbrook Auto Care for brake work, and on September 13 they charged $1,480.00, appearing on your September 23, 2026 statement, without checking with you beforehand.
Customer: Yes, exactly.
